_README: Opportunistic notes for FUTURE test work, captured while reading code (not a backlog of committed tests). Each entry: where it came from, what was observed, why it matters, and candidate tests. Append-only; promote items into tests/plan/backlog.tsv when scheduled.

notes.source: merge of origin/develop social-auth (AuthContext, WelcomeAuth/SocialProfile screens, server/social-auth-handler.ts)
notes.observation: Google + Apple sign-in were added with no test coverage. New users land in a social_auth_pending state and must complete a SocialProfileScreen (gender, date_of_birth) before the account is usable.
notes.why_it_matters: OAuth/native sign-in is hard to automate (system webviews, real accounts) but the pending->complete transition and the server token exchange ARE testable at the API layer.
candidate_tests: headless: social-auth-handler accepts a valid (mocked) Google idToken and creates a user with google_id set, social_auth_pending=true
headless: completing the social profile (gender + dob) flips social_auth_pending=false and issues a usable JWT
headless: an Apple idToken without email is accepted only for an existing apple_id (matches develop commit dbd7011)
e2e (entry-point only): the Google and Apple buttons render and are reachable on WelcomeAuthScreen

notes.source: implication of adding Apple Sign In
notes.observation: Adding 'Sign in with Apple' triggers App Store review requirements the app may not yet satisfy: (a) Apple's 'Hide My Email' relay must be handled (email may be a privaterelay.appleid.com address), (b) where any third-party login exists Apple requires Sign in with Apple be offered too (satisfied), (c) App Store now mandates in-app account deletion.
notes.why_it_matters: These are reviewer-blocking, not optional. The relay-email case affects emailHash uniqueness and any email-based dedup (server uses email_hash unique).
candidate_tests: headless: a privaterelay.appleid.com email is stored/hashed without colliding and without breaking duplicate-email detection
headless/e2e: in-app account deletion exists and actually deletes (or anonymizes) the user

notes.source: qa:provision drizzle-kit push during the merge reconcile
notes.observation: migrations/0009_add_social_auth_fields.sql creates PARTIAL unique indexes (users_google_id_unique ... WHERE google_id IS NOT NULL), but shared/schema.ts declares googleId/appleId with .unique() (a FULL unique constraint). drizzle-kit push therefore sees drift and wants to add a full constraint (prompting to truncate users).
notes.why_it_matters: The migration and the ORM schema definition disagree, so `drizzle-kit push` is not a no-op against a migration-built DB. This is a latent footgun for anyone using db:push and for the schema-drift gate baseline.
candidate_tests: infra: assert the migration-built schema and a drizzle-push schema converge (no pending drift) for the users uniqueness constraints
decision needed: standardize on partial vs full unique for google_id/apple_id and make migration + schema.ts agree

notes.source: mobile/src reading during recon (ExploreScreen, api.service.ts, AuthContext, crashReporter)
notes.observation: App assumes connectivity for all user data. Only the crash reporter has a NetInfo offline queue; there is no offline cache/queue for bubbles, events, or images. On network failure ExploreScreen renders a generic empty state (no offline messaging/retry) and images silently blank. AuthContext.refreshUser is the one graceful path (keeps cached profile).
notes.why_it_matters: User-reported: app is largely non-functional offline (bubbles you belong to vanish, icons missing). Out of scope to FIX now (characterize-state PR); these document current behavior so a fix can be regression-tested.
candidate_tests: characterization e2e/unit: with the network down, ExploreScreen shows an offline-distinct state (currently it does NOT) — mark known-fail until fixed
unit: api.service surfaces a typed offline error rather than a bare throw

notes.source: tests/e2e/auth/auth-0200-signup.yaml (this branch) vs the new signup screens
notes.observation: auth-0200 was updated to drive gender/DOB picker steps (button-select-gender, button-select-dob) that correspond to the new social-signup fields, but those testIDs are unverified against the merged WelcomeAuth/SocialProfile screens (native e2e deferred this session).
notes.why_it_matters: If the new screens lack those testIDs, the flow fails on selectors, not logic — exactly the 'mainly bad-selectors' category to triage when native e2e runs.
candidate_tests: verify (Maestro MCP) that button-select-gender / button-select-dob / input-name exist on the merged signup path before counting auth-0200 as a real failure
